lead: An inclined plane is any cut through a stressed body that is not one of the original x or y faces. The same material carries different normal and shear stresses on that cut. Engineers need these values because a crack, a weld or a shaft keyway may fail on a plane that is not horizontal or vertical. Force equilibrium on a small wedge gives σn and τnt as functions of 2θ. The result explains why a tensile bar yields on a 45° plane and why a thin cylinder under pressure is checked in two directions.
prereq: You need: 2.1 States of stress and Unit 1 equilibrium of forces.

sections.h3: The plane, its normal and the angle θ

blocks.text: Take a point in a body under plane stress. The x face is the face whose outward normal is +x. On it the normal stress is σx (MPa) and the shear stress is τxy (MPa). On the y face the normal stress is σy and the shear stress is the same τxy. Draw a cut through the point. Its outward normal n makes an angle θ with the +x axis, measured counterclockwise. The plane itself is perpendicular to n. At θ=0 the plane is the x face, so σn=σx and τnt=τxy. Some syllabi say θ is measured from the x face; this means the normal turns from +x towards +y.

The stress on this cut has two parts. The normal stress σn acts along n; it is positive when tensile. The shear stress τnt acts along t, which is n rotated 90° counterclockwise; it is positive in the +t direction. On the x face at θ=0, +t is +y, which is the usual positive shear.
σn = (σx + σy)/2 + (σx − σy)/2 · cos2θ + τxy · sin2θ ;  τnt = −(σx − σy)/2 · sin2θ + τxy · cos2θ
blocks.where: σx and σy are normal stresses on the x and y faces in MPa; τxy is the shear stress on those faces in MPa; θ is the angle from the +x axis to the outward normal n, positive counterclockwise; σn is the normal stress on the inclined plane in MPa, positive tensile; τnt is the shear stress on that plane in MPa along t, positive along t. Some syllabi call τnt the shear stress on the inclined plane.

blocks.text: Cut a small triangular wedge at the point. The inclined face has area A and normal n. The x face has area A cosθ and the y face has area A sinθ. Stresses are constant because the wedge is small.
The x-face force is σx A cosθ along x plus τxy A cosθ along y. The y-face force is τxy A sinθ along x plus σy A sinθ along y. The inclined face carries σn A along n and τnt A along t.

Resolve along n = (cosθ, sinθ). The x-face contribution is σx A cos²θ + τxy A sinθ cosθ. The y-face contribution is τxy A sinθ cosθ + σy A sin²θ. Divide by A: σn = σx cos²θ + σy sin²θ + 2τxy sinθ cosθ. Use cos²θ = (1 + cos2θ)/2, sin²θ = (1 − cos2θ)/2 and 2 sinθ cosθ = sin2θ. This gives the first equation above.

Resolve along t = (−sinθ, cosθ). The result is τnt = −(σx − σy) sinθ cosθ + τxy(cos²θ − sin²θ), which is the second equation above. The 2θ terms repeat every 180°. The opposite face has opposite traction, but because t also reverses, τnt has the same value; τnt changes sign when θ increases by 90°.

For a uniaxial field, set σx=σ, σy=0 and τxy=0. Then σn=σ cos²θ and τnt=−σ sinθ cosθ=−(σ/2) sin2θ. At θ=0: σn=σ, τnt=0. At θ=45°: σn=σ/2, τnt=−σ/2. At θ=90°: both are zero. The largest shear magnitude is σ/2 on the 45° planes. A mild steel tensile specimen shows slip lines near 45° for this reason.

For a biaxial field with τxy=0, σn=σx cos²θ + σy sin²θ and τnt=−(σx−σy) sinθ cosθ. If σx=σy=σ, then σn=σ on every plane and τnt=0. Equal tension in two directions creates no in-plane shear. A thin spherical pressure vessel is close to this state; see Unit 7, Thin and Thick Cylinders.

When τxy is not zero, the term τxy sin2θ adds to σn. A shear stress on the x face therefore changes the normal stress on a tilted plane. Students often remember the τxy effect in τnt but omit the τxy sin2θ term from σn. Keep the sign of τnt. A negative value means the shear acts opposite to t; its magnitude is positive. Do not change the formula to make the answer positive.

figure.caption: Normal stress σn and shear stress τnt against θ for σx=80 MPa, σy=40 MPa and τxy=30 MPa. At θ=30° the normal stress is about 96 MPa and the shear is small and negative; at θ=45° the shear reaches −20 MPa.

spec.title: Normal and shear stress vs angle
spec.aria: Two curves show normal stress and shear stress on a plane as the angle theta moves from 0 to 90 degrees.

examples.question: A plane stress state has σx=80 MPa, σy=40 MPa and τxy=30 MPa. Find the normal stress σn and shear stress τnt on a plane at θ=30° from the x face.
steps: Data: σx=80 MPa, σy=40 MPa, τxy=30 MPa, θ=30°, so 2θ=60°.
Mean stress = (σx+σy)/2 = (80+40)/2 = 60 MPa. Half difference = (σx−σy)/2 = (80−40)/2 = 20 MPa.
The negative sign means the shear acts opposite to t. Its magnitude is 2.32 MPa.
examples.answer: The normal stress is 95.98 MPa (tension) and the shear stress is −2.32 MPa, a magnitude of 2.32 MPa acting opposite to t.
examples.check:
import math
sx=80.0
sy=40.0
txy=30.0
theta=30.0
a=math.radians(2*theta)
sn=(sx+sy)/2+(sx-sy)/2*math.cos(a)+txy*math.sin(a)
tnt=-(sx-sy)/2*math.sin(a)+txy*math.cos(a)
print(f"{sn:.2f}")
print(f"{tnt:.2f}")

traps: Putting θ, not 2θ, inside cos and sin. The double angle is 2θ.
Measuring θ from the y face. Then θ=0 would give σy, not σx, and the formulas no longer match.
Dropping τxy sin2θ from σn. A shear on the x face produces normal stress on a tilted plane.
Changing the sign of τnt because it came out negative. Negative only gives direction opposite to t.
Using degrees in a calculator set to radians. 2θ=60° is 1.047 rad, not 60.

quiz.q: State the two transformation equations for σn and τnt on a plane whose normal is at θ from +x.
quiz.a: σn = (σx+σy)/2 + (σx−σy)/2 cos2θ + τxy sin2θ; τnt = −(σx−σy)/2 sin2θ + τxy cos2θ.

quiz.q: Why does a uniaxial bar have maximum shear at θ=45°?
quiz.a: τnt=−(σ/2) sin2θ. Its magnitude is largest when sin2θ=±1, so 2θ=90° and θ=45°.

quiz.q: A uniaxial stress field has σx=120 MPa, σy=0 and τxy=0. Find σn and τnt at θ=30°.
For σx=80 MPa, σy=40 MPa and τxy=30 MPa, find τnt at θ=0° and θ=45°.
quiz.a: At θ=0°, τnt=τxy=30 MPa. At θ=45°, sin90°=1 and cos90°=0, so τnt=−(80−40)/2=−20 MPa.

quiz.q: Equal biaxial stress σx=σy=100 MPa, τxy=0. Show that no plane whose normal lies in the xy plane carries in-plane shear and σn=100 MPa on all such planes.
quiz.a: σn=100 cos²θ+100 sin²θ=100 MPa on every such plane. τnt=−(100−100)/2 sin2θ=0. No plane whose normal lies in the xy plane carries in-plane shear, and σn=100 MPa on all such planes.

quiz.q: A student uses 30° in cos2θ but 60° in sin2θ. Which stress is wrong and why?
quiz.a: Both σn and τnt are wrong in general. In each formula cos2θ must use the same angle 2θ=60° as sin2θ; using 30° gives cos30° instead of cos60°. If a specific state has τxy=0, the cos2θ term in τnt vanishes, but the general answer is both.

quiz.q: State the sign convention for θ and for positive τnt.
quiz.a: θ is positive counterclockwise from +x to the outward normal n. Positive τnt acts along t, which is n rotated 90° counterclockwise.

beyond: Not for the exam. Stress transformation is coded in finite element software at every Gauss point; the same equations convert a computed stress tensor to a local material axis in a composite laminate. Fracture mechanics uses inclined-plane shear to find the direction of a crack under mixed-mode loading. Strain rosettes invert the strain transformation to recover εx, εy and γxy; Hooke's law then gives σx, σy and τxy. Search for Cauchy stress tensor, stress transformation, and mixed-mode crack initiation angle.
